t:
(a) Any participant or former participant in the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System who on February 15, 1981, has a former spouse may, by a spousal agreement, elect to receive a reduced annuity and provide a survivor annuity for such former spouse under section 814(b).
 
    (b) 
        (1) 
If the participant or former participant has not retired under such system on or before February 15, 1981, an election under this section may be made at any time before retirement.
 
        (2) 
If the participant or former participant has retired under such system on or before February 15, 1981, an election under this section may be made within such period after February 15, 1981, as the Secretary of State may prescribe.
 
        (3) For purposes of applying chapter 8 of title I, any such election shall be treated the same as if it were a spousal agreement under section 820(b)(1).
  
    (c) An election under this section may provide for a survivor benefit based on all or any portion of that part of the annuity of the participant which is not designated or committed as a base for survivor benefits for a spouse or any other former spouse of the participant. The participant and his or her spouse may make an election under section 806(b)(1)(B) prior to the time of retirement for the purpose of allowing an election to be made under this section.
 
    (d) The amount of the reduction in the participant’s annuity shall be determined in accordance with section 806(b)(2). Such reduction shall be effective as of—

        (1) 
the commencing date of the participant’s annuity, in the case of an election under subsection (b)(1), or
 
        (2) 
February 15, 1981, in the case of an election under subsection (b)(2).
  
    (e) For purposes of this section, the terms “former spouse”, “participant”, and “spousal agreement” have the meanings given such terms in sections 803 and 804.

fable.w: The tempting reading treats "participant" and "spousal agreement" as signs of participation, but these are only terms for members of a federal retirement system and a private benefits election. The section lets an annuitant choose a reduced annuity to fund a survivor benefit for a former spouse, which is a benefits matter and not outside input into a federal decision. The Secretary of State's power to "prescribe" an election period is a minor administrative deadline with no explicit rulemaking, comment, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue, though it is the one point that leaves some doubt.
fable.s: Any participant or former participant in the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System who on February 15, 1981, has a former spouse may, by a spousal agreement, elect to receive a reduced annuity and provide a survivor annuity for such former spouse

opus.w: The section lets Foreign Service retirement participants choose a reduced annuity to fund a survivor annuity for a former spouse. That is an individual benefit election, which falls under the exception for benefit applications. The Secretary's power to 'prescribe' an election period is a narrow administrative step, not an explicit grant of authority to issue regulations. 'Participant' and 'spousal agreement' are defined terms, and neither brings an outside party into a federal policy decision.
opus.s: an election under this section may be made within such period after February 15, 1981, as the Secretary of State may prescribe.
opus.b:
The section is about individual annuity elections, which fall under the benefits exception, so I've labelled it **No** (about 72% confident).

- **Tempting readings:** Three things could look like participation. The word "participant" appears throughout, and the section mentions a "spousal agreement." It also says the Secretary of State "may prescribe" the election period, which could be read as authority to make rules.
- **Why they fail:** "Participant" just means a member of the retirement system. The spousal agreement is a private choice between a retiree and a former spouse about their own benefits. No outside party is consulted on any federal policy decision.
- **The main risk:** The "may prescribe" wording is a narrow administrative power to set a deadline. It does not explicitly grant authority to issue regulations, unlike the "by regulation" wording in Example 6. If that wording is read as rulemaking authority, the answer would flip to Yes, which is why my confidence is not higher.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes the process for participants in a federal retirement system to elect specific benefit options (reduced annuity, survivor benefits) via a spousal agreement. The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' Since this is a mechanism for claiming or adjusting personal benefits rather than a process for outside parties to influence federal policy or decision-making, it is not participation.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Any participant or former participant in the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System who on February 15, 1981, has a former spouse may, by a spousal agreement, elect to receive a reduced annuity and provide a survivor annuity for such former spouse under section 814(b).
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves an agreement between a participant and their spouse.
Resolution: This is an application for benefits (retirement annuity adjustments). The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits.
